newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Dec 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Dec 12.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Thursday:
- Mutual fund investors jumped into last month's market rallies with both feet, adding significantly to their holdings in stock and bond funds.
- The General Motors Corp said German prosecutors had indicted a former G.M. executive who switched to Volkswagen AG on charges of embezzlement and theft of confidential documents.

- Traders and analysts say a case of the jitters explains why stock prices around the world plunged, interest rates surged and the dollar fell, even though the economic fundamentals that underlie market performance still seem generally positive.
- Prices of treasury securities dropped sharply yesterday amid concern that interest rates could rise if foreign investors slowed their buying.
- Microsoft and Pointcast have become allies in the fast-growing area known as Internet broadcasting.
- Women passed a milestone in the board room in 1996, for the first time holding more than 10 percent of the directors' seats at the nation's 500 largest companies.
- DuPont joined companies that have contracted out their computing operations to giant technology service specialists.
- The New York Stock Exchange has made a deal with CNNFN to transmit its ticker live instead of on a delayed basis.
- An advisory panel recommended that the Food and Drug Administration approve a new type of diabetes drug that could help some diabetics reduce or stop their insulin injections.
- The Canadian Parlaiment is about to endorse stringent curbs on cigarette marketing.
